items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Then he sent to Lewis Armstrong.

ctx.x: Oh, Chicago. They had him, Hellman Umphrey on the, on the Clown-Eyed. He said, he had a bass. And he said, it was old time fellas. I can't remember them, you know, when he first started out. And then when he left here, he left here with a bunch of fellas from here, you know. Then he sent to Lewis Armstrong. And I said, they stayed together. But he was still living around the corner from here. On the street. And then when his wife come back, after she died, she come right back there, and they're there about six…
Well, she's on Phillip Street now. On Phillip Street?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Well, he had Lewis Armstrong. That was the first one.

ctx.x: Ask him who he would use on second cornet.

Who would he use on second cornet? Well, he had Lewis Armstrong. That was the first one. And then after he got Lewis, he had a couple of more, you know. And then Guy Teller come here. Guy Teller was that next to Lewis Armstrong, you know. I was with him a long time too. Guy Teller. Yeah. They said he was, you know, almost good as Lewis Armstrong that time. So he had Guy. Well, Guy left him there and he went to Chicago. Somebody in the middle, wasn't he? Chicago. Yeah. He didn't do so good though. No, they say he…
Why not? Ask me if you knew shots.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: And me and Lewis sometimes used to go down, this is called them tunks.

ctx.x: I asked him which came first.

We had some band, too. Most of our jobs called for white people. We said. We was up three years before we could play for one color people. And the first time we played for color people when Joe Oliver left from the air. You know, the thing I got in there when I was standing right by Joe Oliver with a fellow drumming him, Buddy Sali. Hit him in the eye with a wheel by the hammer. And you know, I thought Joe would be one eye, you know. And he used to have a man, Carol, all them boys. He must have been around about…
I asked you who this Bourne was. That's not Harrison Bourne.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: But still him and Louie was Buddy. Louie come down there when he died.

ctx.x: No. Louie never gives Buddy credit.

He said Louie never gives Buddy no credit. No. But Buddy was a good trumpet player. I hope to tell you. And Buddy could read too. Read yeah. Buddy kept out that liquor. Buddy used to put that music up there sometimes. Surprised as old. And he didn't like to read but he liked to play off. You know about that all the time. But still him and Louie was Buddy. Louie come down there when he died. Once his children was poor about it. I was playing with him then. Buddy put up some music one night and told Zeb if he…
Which pen is that you're talking about?
